title: MSFA-Net and Balmer-line fitting identify 3,583 new blue horizontal-branch stars
summary: A two-stage deep-learning pipeline searched LAMOST DR12 spectra and retained 27,853 BHB candidate spectra. After removal of previously known objects, stringent Balmer-line-profile fitting, and deduplication, the authors report 3,583 unique newly identified blue horizontal-branch stars. Gaia photometry provides an additional consistency check.
ai_technology: MSFA-Net, a multi-scale and frequency-attention deep neural network, followed by a binary refinement classifier
organization: National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A two-stage deep-learning pipeline searched LAMOST DR12 spectra and retained 27,853 BHB candidate spectra.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The paper says high-confidence objects were identified by Balmer-line profile fitting and Gaia color-magnitude consistency, while acknowledging that a fraction could still be contaminants; some atmospheric-parameter outliers are attributed to inference systematics. Counts are unique objects after deduplication, not 3,923 spectra.
evidence.ai_role: MSFA-Net searched the LAMOST DR12 hot-star spectral domain, used staged classification to reduce the spectra to candidate sets, and aided construction of the new sample; Balmer-line profile criteria and duplicate removal yielded the reported 3,583 unique objects. A separate SLAM model estimated atmospheric parameters rather than serving as the confirmation step.
